title: You're Not in Trouble: The ADHD Guide to Building Healthy, Connected Relationships
description: An empowering self-coaching guide to help ADHDers understand, repair, and build healthy relationships—with friends, romantic partners, family, and at work—from ADHD coach Kristen Carder, host of the I Have ADHD podcast and founder of FOCUSED "A compassionate, practical guide for navigating ADHD in all kinds of relationships—from family to friendship to work.” —Adam Grant, #1 New York Times–bestselling author of Vibe and Think Again When you have a neurodivergent brain, it can be hard to connect with the people closest to you. There are rules that everyone else seems to know and play by that don’t come easily to you. Instead of feeling secure and grounded, you move through your relationships feeling like you’re always in trouble . This book provides a solution. In You’re Not in Trouble , Kristen Carder explores how ADHD can shape the five most prominent relationship structures: friendships, work relationships, romantic partnerships, parent-child relationships, and family-of-origin relationships. Armed with this insight, you can begin to build relationships that feel safe, steady, and genuinely connected. You will have practical tools to repair what has been strained, step out of dysfunction, and show up with clarity and self-trust in the relationships that matter most. You’ll learn how to: Regulate your emotions, Prioritize your relationships, Understand and communicate your needs, Understand rejection sensitivity and how to soothe it, and Cultivate connection with yourself and others. This is a gentle journey into connection, without the tired neurotypical advice that never quite fits your ADHD brain. description: Discover practical, hope-filled strategies for building trust, connection, and healing in your family. If you're parenting an adopted child, foster child, or a child from a difficult background, this trusted resource will help you strengthen attachment, address challenging behaviors, and create a more connected home. Traditional parenting approaches often fall short when children have experienced trauma, loss, neglect, or disrupted attachment. In The Connected Parent , renowned child-development expert Dr. Karyn Purvis and adoptive mother Lisa Qualls provide practical tools and compassionate guidance to help parents understand their children's unique needs and respond with confidence, connection, and care. Parents will learn how to: • Encourage secure attachment and healthy family relationships • Respond effectively to challenging behaviors and emotional struggles • Use practical scripts and strategies to simplify everyday interactions • Help children overcome fear, anxiety, and insecurity • Create an environment where healing, trust, and connection can grow Drawing on decades of clinical research, real-world experience, and proven Trust-Based Relational Intervention® (TBRI®) principles, the authors offer actionable solutions that parents can begin using right away. title: Avoidant Attachment Reset: Stop Emotional Shutdowns, Stay Connected Without Losing Yoursel
description: You Don't Have to Choose Between Love and Freedom Maybe relationships feel exciting at first - until someone gets too close. Suddenly, messages feel demanding, affection feels intrusive, and the person you once wanted begins to irritate you. You crave space. You shut down. You question your feelings. Sometimes you leave, only to realize later how much the relationship mattered. Avoidant Attachment Reset is a practical, compassionate guide for anyone who wants connection but fears losing themselves inside it. Instead of telling you to become more dependent, endlessly vulnerable, or available all the time, this book helps you understand why distance can feel so safe—and how to create space without disappearing. Inside, you will learn how to: Recognize the triggers and beliefs behind emotional withdrawal Catch the urge to escape before it makes the decision for you Understand what is happening in your body and emotions Ask for space without shutting someone out Tell the difference between attachment activation and genuine relationship problems Receive support without feeling weak, trapped, or indebted Repair after distance and return to connection Build greater security without sacrificing your independence You do not need to become someone who never needs distance. You just need to stop letting distance make every decision for you.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_4"]', '#CardInstance7s8kx65auL4aisj3dKMP5A')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_4',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode

title: The Calm & Connected Parent: An Attachment-First Guide to Raising Resilient Kids in the Ag
description: Tired of the cycle- ask, repeat, yell, regret? You’re not alone. With constant pings, packed schedules, and big feelings, parenting today can feel impossible. Written by Todd Sarner, MFT, psychotherapist, parenting coach, and founder of Transformative Parenting, this warm, science-based guide draws from over two decades of clinical experience and mentorship with attachment pioneer Dr. Gordon Neufeld, where Sarner also served as a former Faculty Member of the Neufeld Institute. The core truth: your child doesn’t need perfect parents, they need to feel genuinely connected to you in the moments that matter most. When that connection is secure, cooperation, resilience, and healthy maturity naturally follow. Inside, you’ll learn how to: • Create emotional safety and secure attachment your child can truly rely on the foundation for everything else • Navigate screens and AI without losing connection or your authority as their guide • Lead with calm confidence using firm, warm boundaries that teach rather than punish • Turn defiance and meltdowns into opportunities for trust, growth, and real skills • Repair without shame when things go wrong (because they will) • Build three essential capacities in your child creativity, resilience, and wisdom through daily rhythms, not forced outcomes This isn’t permissive “anything goes,” and it isn’t authoritarian control. It’s the middle path of attachment-first leadership steady, warm, and clear. The kind of parenting that brings less chaos, more cooperation, and a home that feels safe and sane again. Most parenting advice treats symptoms. This book strengthens the foundation so discipline, screen boundaries, and emotional regulation flow naturally from secure connection, not compliance tactics. Lead with love. Guide with confidence. Rais

title: Attached: The New Science of Adult Attachment and How It Can Help You Find--and Keep-- Lov
description: Discover how an understanding of adult attachment—the most advanced relationship science in existence today—can help us find and sustain love “Over a decade after its publication, one book on dating has people firmly in its grip.” — The New York Times We already rely on science to tell us what to eat, when to exercise, and how long to sleep. Why not use science to help us improve our relationships? In this revolutionary book, psychiatrist and neuroscientist Dr. Amir Levine and psychologist Rachel Heller scientifically explain why some people seem to navigate relationships effortlessly, while others struggle through adult attachment. Pioneered by psychologist John Bowlby in the 1950s, the field of attachment posits that everyone behaves in one of three distinct ways while in a relationship: • Anxious people are often preoccupied with their relationships and tend to worry about their partner's ability to love them back • Avoidant people equate intimacy with a loss of independence and constantly try to minimize closeness • Secure people feel comfortable with intimacy and are usually warm and loving Attached guides readers in determining what attachment style they and their mate (or potential mate) follow, offering a road map for building stronger, more fulfilling connections with the people they love.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_5"]', '#CardInstanceQjTTJIpwzmL4fo3bnqQLaA')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_5',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,non

title: The Connected Life Method: A Practical System for Building Deeper Relationships, Real Comm
description: The average adult, asked to name the people they could turn to for something that really matters, now answers with a number close to zero. We have never had more ways to reach each other — and we have never felt further apart. If you've ever sat in a room full of people and felt completely alone, or realized you can't remember the last time you felt truly known, this book is for you. The Connected Life Method is not another collection of vague tips about "putting yourself out there." It's a complete, practical system — built from real evidence and years of real conversations — for closing the gap between the connection you have and the connection you actually need. You do not need to be extraordinary to build a connected life. You need a method — and the willingness to use it, one small, deliberate choice at a time. This book is that method. Irene Vans writes about connection, belonging, and the practical psychology of a well-lived life. title: Connected Revenue: Why Relationships Are Worth More Than Appointments
description: Most practices manage what's above the gumline. The value is below it. Your patients spend about three hours a year in your chairs. For the other 8,757, most practices go quiet. That silence is where diagnosed care goes unfinished, loyal patients drift away, and referrals never happen. And in the absence of your professional guidance, patients fill the gap with search results, AI answers, and products no dentist ever recommended. In Connected Revenue , Dr. Bryan Laskin shows how dental practices and the organizations that lead them grow by making one thing easier at every step of the patient relationship: before, during and between appointments. Whether you lead two locations or two thousand, it comes down to Eight Revenue Breakthroughs™, one scorecard, and a new way to see the value already inside your practices. This isn't about squeezing more out of patients. It's about removing the friction that keeps them from getting the care they already want from people they already trust. title: Connected: The Surprising Power of Our Social Networks and How They Shape Our Lives
description: Celebrated scientists Nicholas Christakis and James Fowler explain the amazing power of social networks and our profound influence on one another's lives. Your colleague's husband's sister can make you fat, even if you don't know her. A happy neighbor has more impact on your happiness than a happy spouse. These startling revelations of how much we truly influence one another are revealed in the studies of Dr. Christakis and Fowler, which have repeatedly made front-page news nationwide. In Connected , the authors explain why emotions are contagious, how health behaviors spread, why the rich get richer, even how we find and choose our partners. Intriguing and entertaining, Connected overturns the notion of the individual and provides a revolutionary paradigm-that social networks influence our ideas, emotions, health, relationships, behavior, politics, and much more.
